chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: 'Yahya ibn Suleym al-Ta'i informed me,' who said: 'Amr ibn Shimr al-Yamani narrated, raising the hadith to Ali (peace be upon him):'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Patience is of three types: patience at the time of calamity, patience in performing obedience, and patience in avoiding disobedience. So whoever is patient during the calamity until he repels it with the goodness of his consolation, Allah will write for him three hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance between the sky and the earth. And whoever is patient in performing obedience, Allah will write for him six hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance from the edges of the earth to the Throne. And whoever is patient in avoiding disobedience, Allah will write for him nine hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance from the edges of the earth to the utmost limit of the Throne.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of patience mentioned in Shia hadith and their respective rewards?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi categorizes patience into three hierarchical levels, elevating restraint from sin (sabr 'an al-ma'siyah) as the highest virtue with the greatest reward. It reflects the Shia emphasis on active spiritual discipline, where enduring trials and maintaining obedience are seen as means to attain specific, measurable degrees of proximity to the Divine Throne.
